claims.statement: In an eligible ordinary tree with |T|=2p+2, if every selected original leaf v has component marks in H_v=T-{v,s_v} orderable so that the first mark has H_v-degree at least 2 and the second, when present, has H_v-degree at least 1, then the complete selected sum S(T,p) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: First-order shell |T|=2p+2 under the primary eligibility and fixed strict favorable selector; sufficient per-selected-tag component-root degree condition as stated.
claims.reason: The ordered first-mark partition is exact. Under the stated condition every residual graph J_i has at most 2k-1 vertices for k=p-1, and the independent-set shadow incidence gives i_k(J_i)<=i_{k-1}(J_i). Summing over all roots and all selected original leaf tags proves the claimed full-sum subclass.

claims.statement: The complete favorable-leaf sum is nonpositive for every eligible ordinary tree with |T|=2p+2.
claims.scope: Registered first-order shell: ordinary finite tree T, p with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, fixed F(T,p) defined by Delta_p(T-v)<0, and original supports and neighborhoods.
claims.reason: The ordered-root decomposition proves a sufficient subclass and localizes all terms not controlled by the ordinary shadow bound to first-root degree-one cases and second-root isolate cases at order 2k. The report derives their exact excess but establishes no selector-conditioned cross-root or cross-support compensation, so the registered full shell claim is unresolved.

limitations: The selector has not been shown to force the stated root-degree subclass.
No global compensation inequality for the order-2k boundary excesses is proved.
No counterexample, exhaustive computation, external theorem application, or formal verification is supplied; the full shell claim remains open.
